**Finding: Compliant — no restrictive covenant on Customer (no redline proposed).**

The NONCOMPETE rule is met at the **preferred position** ("No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer") by simple absence.

What I checked and why the apparent hits are not restrictions:

| Search term | Result |
|---|---|
| compete | Only "court of competent jurisdiction" (p0335, p0469) — forum boilerplate |
| competing / shall not engage / field of use / territor / similar business / solicit | No matches |
| exclusiv | Cap Collateral Account control notices (p0387–p0388); "nonexclusive jurisdiction" (p0427) |
| restrict | No-contravention reps (p0240, p0266, p0279); Successor Servicer information carve-out (p0346) |

The two "exclusive" provisions are securities-account control mechanics, not market restrictions, and the "restrict" hits are ordinary representations *referencing* pre-existing third-party restrictions — p0346 actually narrows a disclosure obligation rather than constraining our business. The section outline confirms there is no covenants article where a restrictive covenant would otherwise sit.

Direction check: nothing in the document limits what products or services Verizon Owner Trust 2020-A or Verizon ABS LLC may buy, build, market or operate, so there is no restriction on our party to delete or narrow to the fallback.

One drafting note for your file rather than a redline: because the Issuer and Depositor are special-purpose entities whose permitted activities are already tightly circumscribed by their organizational and transaction documents, any later attempt by Cellco to add a field-of-use or non-compete covenant should be resisted as unnecessary — the walk-away trigger here would be an undefined-scope or post-term restriction exceeding 12 months.
